newsitem.title: FINLAND: Wary Finnish shares fall in international trend.
newsitem.headline: Wary Finnish shares fall in international trend.

text.p: Finnish shares fell on Friday as Wall Street's jitters spread woes on European bourses and bond markets awaited news from the Dublin summit about the EU's planned stability pact, brokers said.
The HEX general index fell 1.75 pct to 2,394.76 points, down ten percent in a yo-yo week.
The forestry sector trimmed recent gains with a sharp decline after pulp stocks were reported above expectations, denting hopes for price hikes.
Pulp producer Metsa-Botnia said it would refrain from a planned pulp price hike to $610 from $560 and Swedish forestry group Assidoman said planned pulp price hikes were unlikely.
The forestry sub-index shed two percent with Metsa-Serla the biggest loser, down five percent or 1.60 markka at 31.70. UPM-Kymmene was liveliest, down 1.50 markka at 92.70.
Nokia ended the week 11 markka lower at 255.00 markka, down three percent for the day from Thursday's 263.00 close, on foreign selling pressure, brokers said.
An announcement from Nokia and UPM-Kymmene's about the sale of their chemicals joint venture did not have an impact on either of the shares, brokers said.
